newsitem.title: USA: Abacan $160 mln junk bond deal postponed.
newsitem.headline: Abacan $160 mln junk bond deal postponed.

text.p: Abacan Resource Corp's $160 million junk bond offering was postponed on Monday after the company announced its 1997 cash flow would fall short of expectations, according to the company.
The postponement came as a joint decision between the company and lead underwriter Bear, Stearns & Co, said Erik Dybesland, high-yield energy analyst at Bear Stearns.

"We've seen recent declines in production, and costs have been up a little bit and that has (made) cash flow to be lower than originally thought," Dybesland said. "So the prudent thing was to delay to see some more production history."
The oil exploration and production company, based in Calgary, Alberta, has assets on the west African coast including its new Ngo No. 6 oil well.
Dybesland said testing of the well within the next couple of weeks should provide a better barometer of future production.

Abacan has said reduced average production, lower world oil prices and higher than expected startup costs were behind the cash flow shortfall. The announcement also sent its stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange down more than four points to 3.98 at 1257 EDT/1657 GMT.
Abacan said it was "reviewing different alternatives to meet its short-term cash requirements."

The postponement follows a string of successful energy-related junk bond deals last week, including $175 million 10-year debt from Snyder Oil Corp; $100 million 10-year debt from Petsec Energy Inc; $120 million 10-year debt from ICO Inc; $200 million 10-year debt from United Refining Co; and $1.5 billion (principal) in two-tranche debt from TransAmerican Energy Corp.
